GX 460 owners report it needs upper control arms, the right offset, a body-mount chop, liner removal and pinch-weld work.

timeline.change: J150 launches in Japan on 14 September and in Australia on 16 November. Debut of KDSS with an electric accumulator, Crawl Control, Multi-Terrain Select and the Multi-Terrain Monitor
Unsealed 4X4 flags launch-year trucks for airbag recalls and electrical gremlins
April: left-hand-drive Prados included in Toyota's VSC software recall after the Lexus GX 460 'Don't Buy' episode
Australian Altitude grade added between GXL and VX

First facelift (Japan 10 Sept, Australia October): new grille, bumpers and lamps, LED low beams, retuned suspension, five-mode MTS. Three-door dropped in Australia. Unsealed 4X4 calls 2013–15 a sweet spot for many buyers: past the early faults and before the DPF
June: 1GD-FTV 2.8 diesel (130 kW / 450 Nm) replaces the 1KD-FTV 3.0. AC60F six-speed auto. DPF arrives. V6 dropped in Japan
Diesels sold October 2015 to April 2020 covered by the Australian DPF class action

Second facelift on 12 September. V6 dropped in Australia. Unsealed 4X4 flags 2017 trucks for head-unit, ESC-light and shift glitches and says not to buy one without paperwork showing they've been fixed
June: manual DPF regeneration switch standard

August update: 150 kW / 500 Nm, 3,000 kg braked towing, auto only, 9-inch screen with CarPlay and Android Auto. Unsealed 4X4 calls 2020–on trucks the most desirable, and 4X4 Australia says this update finally resolved the DPF problem
Production ends in October; replaced by the J250

identify.intro: The 150 was sold under several names and with several engines, and its US twin wears a Lexus badge. The model code tells you what you're looking at.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: KDJ150/155 = 1KD-FTV 3.0 diesel. GDJ150 = 1GD-FTV 2.8 diesel. TRJ150/152 = 2TR-FE 2.7 petrol. GRJ150 = 1GR-FE 4.0 V6. GRJ152 = 3.5 V6 (China). URJ150 = Lexus GX 460. A 155 suffix is the short three-door.

items.head: Market names
items.body: In the UK the J150 was sold as the Land Cruiser LC3, LC4 and LC5 by equipment level. Australian grades were GX, GXL, Altitude (from 2012), VX and Kakadu, plus the three-door SX and ZR until 2013.

items.head: Facelift tells
items.body: 2013-on trucks have the larger grille and new lamps. 2017-on trucks have the second face with the vertical-bar grille. 2020-on Australian trucks have the 9-inch CarPlay screen.

items.head: DPF countermeasures
items.body: On a 2015–2020 diesel, look for the manual DPF regeneration switch (standard from June 2018) and ask a Toyota dealer whether the 2020 remedy is recorded against the VIN.

items.head: Spare and sub-tank
items.body: Trucks with the spare on the tailgate keep the 63-litre sub-tank. Under-floor spare versions give it up.

paragraphs: Toyota never sold the Prado 150 in the US. Americans got the Lexus GX 460 instead. NHTSA lets vehicles at least 25 years old be imported without meeting federal standards, and the first 150s were built in late 2009, so they don't become eligible until late 2034.
Until then, a US buyer who wants a J150 should buy a GX 460. Many Prado-specific parts, from the front end to bumpers, have been fitted to GXs by owners on IH8MUD.

maintenance.description: Prado 150 maintenance schedule: Toyota's diesel schedule with oil every 15,000 km, fuel filter and brake fluid every 30,000 km, timing belt at 150,000 km (1KD), plus dusty-road and towing intervals.
maintenance.intro: Toyota New Zealand publishes its diesel service schedule for the Prado, and it's the clearest factory schedule online for the 150. It's built on a 15,000 km / 12-month service with extra items every second, sixth and tenth year. Petrol Prados (2TR, 1GR, and the US-market GX 460's 1UR) follow their own petrol schedules, so check your book.
maintenance.schedule_note: Toyota New Zealand diesel service schedule for diesel Toyotas built from January 2005, which lists the Prado diesel. Whichever comes first, kilometres or years. Confirm with your dealer for your market and VIN.

items: Replace engine oil and oil filter
Inspect drive belts, air filter and cabin filter
Inspect hoses, exhaust, fuel lines and the water sediment accumulator
Check fluid levels, battery, brakes and pads, steering, suspension, tyres and drive shaft joints
Electronic health check and road test
Replace the fuel filter (or sooner if the filter warning light comes on)
Inspect front and rear differential and transfer fluid
Fluid table: differential oil every 30,000 km / 2 years
Inspect manual or automatic transmission fluid
Fluid table: automatic or manual transmission and transfer oil every 90,000 km / 6 years
Replace the timing belt (1KD-FTV 3.0 only; the 2.8 uses a chain)
Replace the brake booster vacuum pump (Euro 5 Prado, per Toyota NZ footnote)
Injector test and service (Toyota guidance as reported by Unsealed 4X4 and Australian Car Reviews)
On the 2.8, ask for a manual DPF regeneration at services (Unsealed 4X4)

maintenance.severe: Toyota NZ's severe schedule: if you tow, carry full loads or work the truck hard, replace engine oil, brake fluid and transmission oil at half the interval and inspect the propeller shaft joints and diff and transfer oil at half the interval. Extended idling or slow driving, and short trips below freezing, halve the oil interval. On unsealed or dusty roads, halve the oil interval, inspect the timing belt and pulleys every 30,000 km, and halve the air filter, brakes and suspension checks. After water crossings, grease the propeller shaft joints within 24 hours and check the diff oil for water. For frequent off-road use, go by engine hours as well as kilometres.
